title: High resolution climate change observations and projections for the evaluation of heat-related extremes
problem: Coarse spatial resolution and systematic biases in existing climate data are insufficient for resolving local, highly-variable hazards like heat stress and drought, particularly in data-sparse regions, and there is a lack of high-resolution data for key variables like WBGTmax and VPD.
method: The authors generate high-resolution climate projections by calculating 'delta' change fields from coarse CMIP6 model ensembles and applying them to perturb high-resolution historical observations of temperature, precipitation, and relative humidity.
task: The task is to develop a high-resolution global dataset of climate observations and projections for evaluating heat-related extremes by perturbing historical observational data with change fields derived from CMIP6 climate model ensembles.

innovation: This paper introduces a high-resolution (0.05°) global dataset of historical climate observations and future projections for heat-related extremes, created by applying CMIP6 model 'deltas' to observational products to generate detailed projections of temperature, precipitation, Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT), and Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD).

The CHC-CMIP6 dataset is partially based on the Climate Hazards Center (CHC) precipitation and temperature products: the Climate Hazards InfraRed Precipitation with Stations (CHIRPS) product21 and the Climate Hazards InfraRed Temperature with Stations (CHIRTS) product 10,22.

The CHC-CMIP6 dataset also includes RH derived using hourly air temperature (Ta) and dewpoint temperature (Td) from the ERA5 reanalysis42 and daily minimum and maximum CHIRTS (CHIRTS-dailyTmin, CHIRTS-dailyTmax).
